rationale:
Split into 4 children with no dependency edges among them. Besides the existing sibling weighted_radial_monotonicity (step 3), steps 0–5 of the supplied proof contain four separable, reusable obligations:
(A) cylinder_weight = steps 0+2. A C¹ weight h with values in [0,1], equal to 1 on {‖q(z−y)‖<τ} and 0 on {‖q(z−y)‖≥2τ}, satisfying the gradient bound (G) with constant M₀/τ, where M₀ = 4L and L bounds |st′|.
(B) radial_cutoff = step 1. The cutoffs φ(s) = st((A²−s)/(A²−1)) for A > 1.
(C) cutoff_integral_tendsto = step 4. Dominated convergence of ∫φ_j(‖z−y‖²/t²)h dμ to ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ.
(D) cylinder_mass_bound = step 5. Comparison with the cylinder masses and conversion to [0,∞].

The parent keeps only the glue:
- Obtain M₀ from (A) and put C := 2^{n+1}(M₀+1), which is the parent's 2^{n+1}(4L+1). Take h from (A) for τ.
- Put η₀ := min{1,(1−ρ)/(2ρ)} and A_j := 1+η₀/(j+1). Then A_j ∈ (1,2], ρA_j ≤ ρ(1+η₀) < 1 and A_j → 1. Take φ_j from (B).
- For every j, the sibling with M := M₀/τ gives Ĩ_j(σ)/σ^n ≤ Ĩ_j(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(M₀/τ+K)ερ.
- Put R := ρ(1+η₀). Then closedBall y R ⊆ ball y 1 ⊆ U is compact, so μ_W(B_R(y)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).
- Apply (C) for t = σ and t = ρ, then le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'. This gives I(σ)/σ^n ≤ I(ρ)/ρ^n + 2^{n+1}(M₀/τ+K)ερ ≤ I(ρ)/ρ^n + C(1+K)ερ/τ. The second step uses τ ≤ 1, which gives M₀ + Kτ ≤ (M₀+1)(1+K).
- Apply (D) with E := C(1+K)ερ/τ and μ_W(B_ρ(y)) ≤ μ_W(B_R(y)) < ∞. This is exactly the frozen conclusion.

(A) uses only st′(u) = 0 for u < 0, which gives ‖q w‖ ≤ 2τ. That suffices for (G), so the facts st′(0) = st′(1) = 0 are not needed.

subproblems.title: C¹ cylindrical weight with tangential gradient bound (steps 0 and 2 of the cylinder-monotonicity proof, Simon 8.5.10 (7))
subproblems.statement: There is a constant M₀ ≥ 0 such that for all N, n ∈ ℕ, every P ∈ G(N,n), every y ∈ ℝ^N and every τ > 0 there is a function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with: (i) h is C¹; (ii) 0 ≤ h(z) ≤ 1 for all z; (iii) h(z) = 1 whenever |q(z − y)| < τ; (iv) h(z) = 0 whenever |q(z − y)| ≥ 2τ; (v) |Dh(z)[p_S(z − y)]| ≤ (M₀/τ)·t_P(S)·|z − y| for all z ∈ ℝ^N and S ∈ G(N,n). Here ℝ^N = Euclidean N, G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n, p_S = Grassmannian.project S is the orthogonal projection onto S (the linear map projectionLinearMap S), q(v) := v − p_P(v), Dh = fderiv ℝ h, and t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P)‖ is the operator norm of p_S − p_P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∃ M₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ M₀ ∧ ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (τ : ℝ), 0 < τ → ∃ h : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 h ∧ (∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ z, ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < τ → h z = 1) ∧ (∀ z, 2 * τ ≤ ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ → h z = 0) ∧ ∀ (z : Euclidean N) (S : Grassmannian N n), |fderiv ℝ h z (Grassmannian.project S (z - y))| ≤ M₀ / τ * ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S - Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ * ‖z - y‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 2 of the parent proof (Simon 8.5.10, printed (7), where h(z) = f(|q(z − y)|) with f ≡ 1 on [0,τ) and f ≡ 0 on (2τ,∞), and |∇^S f(|q(z − y)|)| ≤ |f′|·|p_S − p|). The parent's h(z) := st(4 − ‖q(z − y)‖²/τ²) is used, and M₀ := 4L, where L bounds |Real.smoothTransition′|; no numerical value of L is needed.
Notation. st := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff), monotone, 0 ≤ st ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), st(u) = 0 for u ≤ 0 (zero_of_nonpos), st(u) = 1 for u ≥ 1 (one_of_one_le). st′ := deriv st.

1. st′ vanishes off [0,1]. If u < 0, then st = 0 on the open neighbourhood (−∞,0) of u, so st′(u) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq, deriv_const). If u > 1, then st = 1 on the open neighbourhood (1,∞) of u, so st′(u) = 0.

2. The constant. st is C¹, so st′ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_deriv). By step 1 the support of st′ lies in the compact set [0,1], so st′ has compact support and is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Fix L with |st′(u)| ≤ L for all u ∈ ℝ. Then L ≥ |st′(0)| ≥ 0. Put M₀ := 4L ≥ 0. It does not depend on N, n, P, y or τ.

3. Set-up. Fix N, n, P, y and τ > 0. Let p := projectionLinearMap P, so p_P(v) = p(v). The map p is self-adjoint (projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (project_project). Let Q := id − p, regarded as a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^N, so Q(v) = v − p_P(v) = q(v). Define F(z) := ‖Q(z − y)‖²/τ² and h(z) := st(4 − F(z)). Note F(z) = ‖q(z − y)‖²/τ².

4. Property (i). z ↦ Q(z − y) is a continuous affine map, hence C^∞. The map v ↦ ‖v‖² is C^∞ (contDiff_norm_sq). Dividing by the constant τ² ≠ 0, subtracting from 4 and composing with the C^∞ function st keep the map C^∞. So h is C^∞, in particular C¹.

5. Property (ii) holds because st takes values in [0,1].

6. Property (iii). If ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ, then ‖q(z − y)‖² < τ² because both sides are non-negative. So F(z) < 1 and 4 − F(z) > 3 ≥ 1, hence h(z) = 1.

7. Property (iv). If ‖q(z − y)‖ ≥ 2τ > 0, then ‖q(z − y)‖² ≥ 4τ², so F(z) ≥ 4 and 4 − F(z) ≤ 0. Hence h(z) = 0.

8. Derivative formula. Fix z and put w := z − y and a := Q w = q(w). The map z′ ↦ Q(z′ − y) has derivative Q at z. By HasFDerivAt.norm_sq, z′ ↦ ‖Q(z′ − y)‖² has derivative v ↦ 2⟨a, Q v⟩, so DF(z)[v] = (2/τ²)⟨a, Q v⟩. The map s ↦ st(4 − s) has derivative −st′(4 − s) at s (chain rule with the derivative −1 of s ↦ 4 − s). By the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt), for all v ∈ ℝ^N:
  Dh(z)[v] = −st′(4 − F(z))·(2/τ²)·⟨a, Q v⟩.

9. Inner-product identity. Let S ∈ G(N,n) and T := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P), so ‖T‖ = t_P(S). Because p is idempotent, p a = p w − p(p w) = 0. For v := p_S w, self-adjointness of p gives
  ⟨a, Q v⟩ = ⟨a, v⟩ − ⟨a, p v⟩ = ⟨a, v⟩ − ⟨p a, v⟩ = ⟨a, v⟩.
 Self-adjointness of p_S gives ⟨a, p_S w⟩ = ⟨p_S a, w⟩, and p_S a = p_S a − p a = T a. Hence ⟨a, Q(p_S w)⟩ = ⟨T a, w⟩. By Cauchy–Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm) and ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm,
  |⟨a, Q(p_S w)⟩| ≤ ‖T a‖·‖w‖ ≤ t_P(S)·‖a‖·‖w‖.

10. Property (v). By steps 8 and 9, |Dh(z)[p_S w]| = |st′(4 − F(z))|·(2/τ²)·|⟨T a, w⟩|.
 – If st′(4 − F(z)) = 0, the left side is 0. The right side (M₀/τ)·t_P(S)·‖w‖ is a product of non-negative numbers, so the bound holds.
 – Otherwise step 1 forces 4 − F(z) ≥ 0, i.e. ‖a‖² ≤ 4τ², so ‖a‖ ≤ 2τ. Using |st′| ≤ L and step 9,
  |Dh(z)[p_S w]| ≤ L·(2/τ²)·t_P(S)·(2τ)·‖w‖ = (4L/τ)·t_P(S)·‖w‖ = (M₀/τ)·t_P(S)·‖z − y‖.
Thus h satisfies (i)–(v). ∎
proof_key_steps: st′ = 0 off [0,1] (st locally constant there); st′ continuous with compact support, so |st′| ≤ L for some L ≥ 0; M₀ := 4L
h(z) := st(4 − ‖q(z − y)‖²/τ²) is C^∞ (contDiff_norm_sq, affine maps) with values in [0,1]
h = 1 where ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ and h = 0 where ‖q(z − y)‖ ≥ 2τ
Chain rule: Dh(z)[v] = −st′(4 − F(z))·(2/τ²)·⟨q w, Q v⟩ with Q = id − p_P, w = z − y
p_P(q w) = 0 and self-adjointness of p_P, p_S give ⟨q w, Q(p_S w)⟩ = ⟨(p_S − p_P)(q w), w⟩, of absolute value ≤ t_P(S)‖q w‖‖w‖
st′(4 − F(z)) ≠ 0 forces ‖q w‖ ≤ 2τ, so |Dh(z)[p_S w]| ≤ (4L/τ)·t_P(S)·‖w‖ = (M₀/τ)·t_P(S)·‖z − y‖

subproblems.title: C¹ non-increasing radial cutoff: 1 on (−∞,1], 0 on [A²,∞) (step 1 of the cylinder-monotonicity proof)
subproblems.statement: For every real number A > 1 there is a function φ : ℝ → ℝ that is C¹, non-increasing, takes values in [0,1], and satisfies φ(s) = 1 for every s ≤ 1 and φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A².
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ A : ℝ, 1 < A → ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ Antitone φ ∧ (∀ s, 0 ≤ φ s ∧ φ s ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ s, s ≤ 1 → φ s = 1) ∧ (∀ s, A ^ 2 ≤ s → φ s = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof, which uses the cutoffs φ_η(s) := st((A_η² − s)/(A_η² − 1)) with A_η = 1 + η. Here the same formula is used for an arbitrary A > 1.
Notation. st := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff), monotone (Real.smoothTransition.monotone), 0 ≤ st ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), st(u) = 0 for u ≤ 0 (zero_of_nonpos), st(u) = 1 for u ≥ 1 (one_of_one_le).

1. Let A > 1 and put d := A² − 1. Since A > 1 > 0 we have A² > 1, so d > 0. Define φ(s) := st((A² − s)/d).

2. C¹. The map s ↦ (A² − s)/d is affine, hence C^∞. Composing it with the C^∞ function st gives a C^∞ function, in particular a C¹ one.

3. Non-increasing. If s ≤ s′, then A² − s′ ≤ A² − s. Dividing by d > 0 gives (A² − s′)/d ≤ (A² − s)/d. Since st is monotone, φ(s′) ≤ φ(s).

4. Range. 0 ≤ φ(s) ≤ 1 for every s, because st takes values in [0,1].

5. Plateau. If s ≤ 1, then A² − s ≥ A² − 1 = d, so (A² − s)/d ≥ 1 and φ(s) = 1.

6. Support. If s ≥ A², then A² − s ≤ 0. A non-positive numerator over the positive d gives (A² − s)/d ≤ 0, so φ(s) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: φ(s) := st((A² − s)/(A² − 1)) with d = A² − 1 > 0
φ is C^∞ (composition of st with an affine map), hence C¹
φ is non-increasing since the affine map is decreasing and st is monotone
0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 from the range of st
φ(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1 (argument ≥ 1) and φ(s) = 0 for s ≥ A² (argument ≤ 0)

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for shrinking radial cutoffs (step 4 of the cylinder-monotonicity proof)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra), y ∈ ℝ^N, and h : ℝ^N → ℝ measurable with 0 ≤ h ≤ 1. For j ∈ ℕ let φ_j : ℝ → ℝ be measurable with 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, φ_j(s) = 1 for every s ≤ 1 and φ_j(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A_j², where A_j > 0 for all j and A_j → 1 as j → ∞. Let t > 0 and R ∈ ℝ with t·A_j ≤ R for all j and μ(B_R(y)) < ∞, where B_r(y) = closedBall y r. Then the Bochner integrals ∫ φ_j(|z − y|²/t²)·h(z) dμ(z) converge, as j → ∞, to the Bochner integral ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (y : Euclidean N) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (φ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (A : ℕ → ℝ) (t R : ℝ), Measurable h → (∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1) → (∀ j, Measurable (φ j)) → (∀ j s, 0 ≤ φ j s ∧ φ j s ≤ 1) → (∀ j s, s ≤ 1 → φ j s = 1) → (∀ j s, A j ^ 2 ≤ s → φ j s = 0) → (∀ j, 0 < A j) → Tendsto A atTop (𝓝 1) → 0 < t → (∀ j, t * A j ≤ R) → μ (closedBall y R) ≠ ∞ → Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ z, φ j (‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) * h z ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ z in closedBall y t, h z ∂μ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof: "By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), Ĩ_{η_j}(t) → I(t) := ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ". The dominating function there is the indicator of a closed ball of finite measure. Here the argument is stated for a general family of cutoffs.
Notation. B_r(y) := closedBall y r, a closed and hence measurable set. Put F_j(z) := φ_j(‖z − y‖²/t²)·h(z), f := 1_{B_t(y)}·h (the indicator of B_t(y) applied to h), and g := 1_{B_R(y)}, the indicator of B_R(y) of the constant 1.

1. Reduction. B_t(y) is measurable, so ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ = ∫ f dμ (integral_indicator). It therefore suffices to show ∫ F_j dμ → ∫ f dμ. This follows from the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence, filter atTop on ℕ) with bound g. Its four hypotheses are verified in steps 2–5.

2. Measurability. z ↦ ‖z − y‖²/t² is continuous, hence measurable. φ_j and h are measurable, so every F_j is measurable and in particular AE strongly measurable.

3. Domination: ‖F_j(z)‖ ≤ g(z) for all j and all z.
 – If z ∈ B_R(y), then 0 ≤ F_j(z) = φ_j(‖z − y‖²/t²)·h(z) ≤ 1·1 = 1 = g(z).
 – If z ∉ B_R(y), then ‖z − y‖ > R ≥ t·A_j > 0, using t > 0 and A_j > 0. Hence ‖z − y‖² > (t·A_j)² = A_j²·t², i.e. ‖z − y‖²/t² ≥ A_j². So φ_j(‖z − y‖²/t²) = 0 and F_j(z) = 0 = g(z).

4. Integrability of g. μ(B_R(y)) < ∞, so the constant 1 is integrable on B_R(y) (integrableOn_const). Since B_R(y) is measurable, its indicator g is integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).

5. Pointwise convergence at every z.
 – If ‖z − y‖ ≤ t, then ‖z − y‖²/t² ≤ 1 (as t > 0). So φ_j(‖z − y‖²/t²) = 1 and F_j(z) = h(z) = f(z) for every j.
 – If ‖z − y‖ > t, then s := ‖z − y‖²/t² > 1. As A_j → 1 we have A_j² → 1 < s, so A_j² ≤ s for all sufficiently large j. For those j, φ_j(s) = 0 and F_j(z) = 0 = f(z).
 In both cases F_j(z) → f(z).

6. By steps 2–5 and dominated convergence, ∫ F_j dμ → ∫ f dμ = ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Rewrite ∫_{B_t(y)} h dμ as ∫ 1_{B_t(y)} h dμ (integral_indicator) and apply dominated convergence with bound 1_{B_R(y)}
Measurability of F_j(z) = φ_j(‖z − y‖²/t²)h(z)
Domination: F_j ∈ [0,1], and F_j(z) = 0 off B_R(y) because ‖z − y‖ > R ≥ tA_j gives ‖z − y‖²/t² ≥ A_j²
1_{B_R(y)} is integrable since μ(B_R(y)) < ∞
Pointwise limit: φ_j(…) = 1 for ‖z − y‖ ≤ t; for ‖z − y‖ > t, A_j² → 1 < ‖z − y‖²/t² makes φ_j(…) = 0 eventually

subproblems.title: From weighted ball integrals to cylinder masses in [0,∞] (step 5 of the cylinder-monotonicity proof)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, P ∈ G(N,n), y ∈ ℝ^N, and q(v) := v − p_P(v) with p_P = Grassmannian.project P. Let τ, σ, ρ, E ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ ≤ ρ and μ(B_ρ(y)) < ∞, where B_r(y) = closedBall y r. Let h : ℝ^N → ℝ be measurable with 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, h(z) = 1 whenever |q(z − y)| < τ, and h(z) = 0 whenever |q(z − y)| ≥ 2τ. Suppose the real inequality (∫_{B_σ(y)} h dμ)/σ^n ≤ (∫_{B_ρ(y)} h dμ)/ρ^n + E holds (Bochner integrals). Then, in [0,∞], μ(B_σ(y) ∩ {z : |q(z − y)| < τ})/ofReal(σ)^n ≤ μ(B_ρ(y) ∩ {z : |q(z − y)| < 2τ})/ofReal(ρ)^n + ofReal(E), where ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal (so ofReal(E) = max(E,0)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (P : Grassmannian N n) (y : Euclidean N) (h : Euclidean N → ℝ) (τ σ ρ E : ℝ), Measurable h → (∀ z, 0 ≤ h z ∧ h z ≤ 1) → (∀ z, ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < τ → h z = 1) → (∀ z, 2 * τ ≤ ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ → h z = 0) → 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → μ (closedBall y ρ) ≠ ∞ → (∫ z in closedBall y σ, h z ∂μ) / σ ^ n ≤ (∫ z in closedBall y ρ, h z ∂μ) / ρ ^ n + E → μ (closedBall y σ ∩ {z | ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < τ}) / ENNReal.ofReal σ ^ n ≤ μ (closedBall y ρ ∩ {z | ‖(z - y) - Grassmannian.project P (z - y)‖ < 2 * τ}) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n + ENNReal.ofReal E
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof: "By step 2(c) and 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, μ(U^τ_σ(y)) ≤ I(σ) and I(ρ) ≤ μ(U^{2τ}_ρ(y)) … Applying ENNReal.ofReal … gives the asserted inequality in [0,∞]". Here the comparison is stated for any h with these properties.
Notation. B_r(y) := closedBall y r. S₁ := {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < τ}, S₂ := {z : ‖q(z − y)‖ < 2τ}, U₁ := B_σ(y) ∩ S₁ and U₂ := B_ρ(y) ∩ S₂. For a set U of finite measure write μ_ℝ(U) := (μ U).toReal (= μ.real U).

1. Borel sets. p_P = projectionLinearMap P is a linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^N, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional). So z ↦ ‖q(z − y)‖ = ‖(z − y) − p_P(z − y)‖ is continuous, and S₁, S₂ are open, hence measurable. Closed balls are measurable.

2. Finiteness. Since σ ≤ ρ, B_σ(y) ⊆ B_ρ(y), so μ(B_σ(y)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)) < ∞. Also μ(U₁) ≤ μ(B_σ(y)) < ∞ and μ(U₂) ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)) < ∞.

3. Integrability. h is measurable with |h| ≤ 1, so h is integrable on every set of finite μ-measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), in particular on B_σ(y), B_ρ(y) and U₂. The constant 1 is integrable on U₂ (integrableOn_const).

4. Lower comparison. h = 1 on U₁ ⊆ S₁, so ∫_{U₁} h dμ = ∫_{U₁} 1 dμ = μ_ℝ(U₁) (setIntegral_congr_fun, setIntegral_const). Since h ≥ 0 and U₁ ⊆ B_σ(y), ∫_{U₁} h dμ ≤ ∫_{B_σ(y)} h dμ (setIntegral_mono_set). Hence μ_ℝ(U₁) ≤ ∫_{B_σ(y)} h dμ.

5. Upper comparison. Split B_ρ(y) along the measurable set S₂ (integral_inter_add_sdiff):
  ∫_{B_ρ(y)} h dμ = ∫_{U₂} h dμ + ∫_{B_ρ(y)∖S₂} h dμ.
 For z ∈ B_ρ(y) ∖ S₂ we have ‖q(z − y)‖ ≥ 2τ, so h(z) = 0, and the second integral is 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). On U₂ we have h ≤ 1, so ∫_{U₂} h dμ ≤ ∫_{U₂} 1 dμ = μ_ℝ(U₂) (setIntegral_mono_on, setIntegral_const). Hence ∫_{B_ρ(y)} h dμ ≤ μ_ℝ(U₂).

6. Real inequality. Since σ^n > 0 and ρ^n > 0, steps 4 and 5 and the hypothesis give
  μ_ℝ(U₁)/σ^n ≤ (∫_{B_σ(y)} h dμ)/σ^n ≤ (∫_{B_ρ(y)} h dμ)/ρ^n + E ≤ μ_ℝ(U₂)/ρ^n + E.

7. Conversion to [0,∞]. Let r > 0 and let U have μ(U) < ∞. Then μ(U) = ofReal(μ_ℝ(U)) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal) and ofReal(r)^n = ofReal(r^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_pow). Since r^n > 0, ofReal(μ_ℝ(U))/ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(μ_ℝ(U)/r^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos). Therefore
  μ(U₁)/ofReal(σ)^n = ofReal(μ_ℝ(U₁)/σ^n)
   ≤ ofReal(μ_ℝ(U₂)/ρ^n + E)   (step 6 and monotonicity of ofReal)
   ≤ ofReal(μ_ℝ(U₂)/ρ^n) + ofReal(E)   (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le)
   = μ(U₂)/ofReal(ρ)^n + ofReal(E).
 Since U₁ and U₂ are exactly the sets in the conclusion, this is the asserted inequality. ∎
proof_key_steps: S₁ = {‖q(z − y)‖ < τ}, S₂ = {‖q(z − y)‖ < 2τ} are open (p_P continuous); all sets involved have finite μ-measure
h is integrable on finite-measure sets (|h| ≤ 1, measurable)
μ(B_σ ∩ S₁) = ∫_{B_σ ∩ S₁} h ≤ ∫_{B_σ} h since h = 1 on S₁ and h ≥ 0
∫_{B_ρ} h = ∫_{B_ρ ∩ S₂} h ≤ μ(B_ρ ∩ S₂) since h = 0 off S₂ and h ≤ 1
Real inequality μ(U₁)/σ^n ≤ μ(U₂)/ρ^n + E
Convert with ofReal_toReal, ofReal_pow, ofReal_div_of_pos and ofReal_add_le
